why: This is the canonical next-greater-element query. Scanning from the right, keep a stack of candidate values that strictly decreases from bottom to top: anything <= the current value can never be anyone's answer again, so pop it; the top that remains is the answer.
hints: The brute force checks every later element. When can a later value never be the next greater element of anything to its left?
When a larger-or-equal value stands before it: from the left, that earlier value blocks it. So the candidates seen from position i always form a decreasing sequence.
Scan from right to left with a stack: pop while top <= nums[i]; answer is the top or -1; push nums[i]. Each value is pushed and popped once, O(n).
pitfalls: Equal values do not count as greater: pop on <=, not <.
The answer is the value, not the index or the distance.
An empty array returns an empty array.
